correctness.rationale: For normalized disjoint AL vectors, the lattice norm gives an isometric ell1 span, so the restricted operator norm is exactly the supremum of image norms. Infinite subsequence selection proves Gamma_d=beta. A tail-block contradiction shows beta≤kappa_d on any Banach lattice with admissible disjoint sequences, while kappa_d≤Gamma_d is immediate. Disjoint spans admit a coordinate AL lattice structure with exactly the ambient disjoint sequences; published Proposition 4.5 gives the symmetric perturbation bound. Every normalization, support, infimum and endpoint has been checked; the identity operator witnesses exact coefficient one.

value.rationale: The paper poses the comparison of kappa_d and beta as an explicit open quantitative question. The theorem answers its full natural abstract AL endpoint class with the optimal coefficient 1, all target Banach spaces and no separability or atomicity assumptions. This is a substantive sharp structural classification of nested operator moduli, with a usable liminf formula and a quantitative stability corollary; it is not asserted to settle the general lattice case.
